uncited: Group Prefix Sum for Shell Lists is a parallel compaction method for shell lists in GPU-based isosurface extraction, replacing sequential thread-0 processing with a parallel prefix sum approach.
It solves the bottleneck of sequentially compacting shell lists by enabling all threads to participate in the compaction process simultaneously.

Unlike standard exclusive prefix sum implementations, this method operates on grouped shell data structures, coordinating with the octree to determine block offsets from the first active octree nodes (AOs) in each shell.
The method processes shell lists in parallel groups, where each group handles a block of 128 functions.
Shell data is packed into chunks of at most 32 AOs, with rows of coefficient matrices (C) staged in groupshared memory for simultaneous reading by all threads in the group.
- Shell list entries: Contain AO offsets and coefficient matrix rows
- Groupshared memory: Stores up to 32 AOs per chunk, with 16 field records uploaded per thread
- Octree offsets: Derived from the first AO of each shell in a block
Load shell list data into groupshared memory, uploading all 16 field records per thread
Clamp loads from groupshared indices to handle inactive lanes (particularly for llvmpipe compatibility)
Compute parallel prefix sum (iso_group_prefix) across the shell list entries
Extract AO offsets from the first AOs of each shell to determine block offsets for the octree
Update shell list entries with compacted positions based on the prefix sum results
- Inactive lanes: Loads from groupshared memory must be clamped to prevent out-of-bounds access
- llvmpipe compatibility: Special handling required for inactive lane loads
- Empty shells: Must handle cases where shells contain no valid AOs
The method enables parallel processing of shell list compaction, significantly improving performance over sequential thread-0 processing.
The use of groupshared memory reduces global memory bandwidth requirements by allowing threads to share data locally.
However, the method requires careful handling of inactive lanes and clamping operations, which may introduce additional computational overhead.
The approach is particularly effective for large shell lists where parallel processing benefits outweigh the coordination costs.
This method originates from the md_gto_iso_gpu optimization work by Scanberg, implemented in the mdlib repository.
The approach represents a shift from sequential to parallel shell list compaction in GPU-based isosurface extraction, improving performance for large-scale volume rendering applications.
The implementation includes specific handling for llvmpipe compatibility and uses environment variables (GTO_ISO_RELAX_FIRST, GTO_ISO_CORNERS_V2) to control behavior.
